The report was true when written and the listener landed 39 MINUTES LATER; I read a dated document as the state of the tree and never ran git log, while THIS FILE's own decisions[0] said "The listener is WRITTEN, not borrowed". A research subagent caught it. (b) On that false premise I put a real decision to the owner — vendor the upstream websocket-to-conn.ts — and he answered it; he reversed it once shown the history. An independent plan check returned FAIL and its BLOCKER was a real hole in the evidence design. The four PeerId readings could not distinguish "survived an eviction" from "was never evicted" — two readings of a live object match trivially — and the DEFAULT made that the likely outcome, not an unlucky one: hibernatable-socket.ts:17-22 records yamux keepAliveInterval 30_000, so a held connection wakes the object every thirty seconds and "hold a connection and wait" was the one procedure GUARANTEED not to evict. The fact was in the tree; nobody had joined it to the runbook. Fixed by TDD in adc9336: GET /self returns a third field `instance`, fixed at construction, so a construction boundary is visible in the readings themselves — 4 cases, 3 watched red first. NOT the 1012 revived-socket path, because whether workerd accepts 1012 is UNVERIFIED in that file's own docblock. Timing mattered: adding it after the single deploy would have cost a second one. Three further findings closed in 4582932 — task_count 0 against two autonomous:false precedents (now 5 tasks, each with verify/done, verify.plan-structure 0 errors 0 warnings); files_modified [] was dishonest since closing flips requirement rows; and no precondition that the namespace holds zero objects, without which "the FIRST object" means nothing. The checker also refuted a candidate: wrangler evictDurableObject is Miniflare's local-dev simulator behind getRuntimeMiniflare, not a lever over a deployed edge object. CLOSED 2026-08-26 in caa46c6 — Phase 30 requirement 4. A revived socket is CLOSED with 1012, not resumed: Noise has no session resumption and yamux no resync, so every alternative is a connection that lies about being live. The registry is keyed by socket identity, so the miss IS the detection. FIVE PLANTS WATCHED RED. The route is wired, so createHostedFabric has a production caller — bundle 583.94 -> 1867.80 KiB, kadDHT 0 -> 11, and diffieHellman/node:crypto STILL 0. §17's claim is deliberately narrowed in the prose: yamux defaults enableKeepAlive at 30 s, so an object under a live connection will not hibernate at all and the proven win is only the six-minute abort. TAMING THE KEEPALIVE IS A NAMED OPEN DECISION, NOT TAKEN — a peer that never sends cannot detect a dead path. Also open and reported: whether workerd accepts 1012 (1011 is known accepted), and whether binaryType may be assigned on a hibernatable socket, deliberately not asserted either way. At 5 000 ms every shard still agreed; at 15 000 ms the frozen dispatches capped at 10001/10001/10000 ms and #21 came back "rpc to ... timed out after 10000ms". THAT IS THE FABRIC BEHAVING CORRECTLY — nothing in production to repair; what was defective is the fixture’s silence about resting on freeze-to-release staying inside the budget. NO NEW ASSERTION, and the reason is measured: the solo dispatch begins after freeze() resolves, so a bound on the span would redden a green run in a ~200 ms band. The span is printed instead. THE PLANT CAUGHT A DEFECT IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT — the first version read thawedAt, the instant the thaw is DECIDED, and printed 764 ms under a 15 000 ms delay; now taken at releasedAt, reading 1381 ms clean and 16 244 ms planted. A TENTH speculation-agents mode. INSTRUMENT LANDED 2026-08-26 in 4909617, CAUSE STILL UNVERIFIED and deliberately so. The symptom: `on.shards.flatMap(s => s.rejections)` came back with one `unreachable: no answer in 2000ms`, seen once in ten runs under eight CPU burners at load 29. It could not be attributed because the fixture printed no frozen ids, and the two readings it could not separate are OPPOSITE — the fixture’s own freeze reaching the admission-offer path (a fixture defect) versus a genuine reading about that path under load. Each refusal now prints the ROLE of the node that gave it: FROZEN(public-victim), FROZEN(paired-owner), FROZEN(solo-owner), FROZEN(unclassified) or healthy. Two plants watched red, one per branch. NOT REPRODUCED SINCE: twelve further runs under eight burners at load up to 235 stayed green, so across both hunts it is ONE redness in TWENTY-TWO runs, and LOAD IS NOT ESTABLISHED AS THE VARIABLE and must not be written down as the cause. CORRECTED 2026-08-26, same day: 4909617’s message says "the single hit came at load 29 while eighteen runs above it were green" and THAT FIGURE IS NOT DEFENSIBLE — per-run load readings exist only for the first hunt (15.95, 29.00 RED, 29.93, 36.01, 41.25, 49.91, 49.37, 49.88, 50.69, 48.90, each taken AFTER its run), while the second hunt recorded only a final 235.70 and began on fresh burners, so an unknown number of its twelve runs were below 29. What survives is weaker and is the whole point: eight green runs in hunt 1 read above the red run’s own reading, twelve more ran green ending at 235, and no per-run figure supports load as the variable. The "load 29" attributed to the red run is itself an after-the-fact reading of a ramp, not a measurement during it. NEXT: keep the instrument, and let the next natural occurrence name the role before any repair is attempted. The 2000 ms is an absolute on the admission-offer path and is where to look once the role is known.

CLOSED 2026-08-26 — git-flow is ENFORCED now, and three holes were measured before being closed. (1) The branch-name rule was a WARNING that printed "Proceeding with commit (not enforced for other branches)": 44 of 108 branches carried names outside its list, so it became a refusal AND the list widened to what the work produces (fix/, chore/, docs/, test/ beside git-flow's own, plus the exact shape worktree-agent-<hex> which is the harness's). (2) NO MERGE WAS EVER CHECKED — git runs pre-merge-commit for an automatic merge and that hook did not exist. (3) The same merge got opposite verdicts depending on whether it conflicted, because a conflicted one is finalised by `git commit` and hit the flat refusal. THE FIRST FIX WAS GREEN ON 26 SPEC CASES AND COMPLETELY INERT, caught only by planting: both forbidden merges went through and both branches moved. Measured with a probe hook — on git 2.33.0 MERGE_HEAD does NOT exist yet at pre-merge-commit and GITHEAD_<sha> does; MERGE_HEAD belongs to the conflicted path, a separate process no GITHEAD survives into. Rules now live in .githooks/git-flow-rules.sh, exercised by packages/node/src/git-flow-rules.node.test.ts (27 cases). ONE ARM CANNOT BE PLANTED AND SAYS SO: develop taking main is a fast-forward and git invokes no merge hook for one; reference-transaction could catch it and is deliberately refused as disproportionate. A FRESH CLONE ALSO HAD ZERO ENFORCEMENT — core.hooksPath lives in .git/config, not in the repository — closed by a `prepare` script.

Ordering is the whole control, and the zero-object check is what makes "the FIRST object" mean anything — an object's location is fixed by its very first get() and the only repair is a new name. Cost is ~$5/month against the owner's $15 budget: 331,776 GB-s against 400,000 included. Criterion 2 needs a REDEPLOY as well, counted as its own act rather than folded into the first; "one deploy" is about criterion 1's ordering only. Pass condition is an AND: every peerId identical AND rows 2 and 3 each carrying an `instance` different from row 1's. An unchanged marker is a "not yet", never a pass. How eviction is FORCED stays UNVERIFIED with one candidate refuted; the redeploy is the certain lever, and if the eviction row cannot be obtained it is reported open rather than covered by the redeploy row.

decisions.decision: The listener is WRITTEN, not borrowed
decisions.rationale: webSocketToMaConn is not on @libp2p/websockets' public surface; reaching it means a path into dist/, a build artefact with no semver signal. The base class comes through @libp2p/utils' public barrel and only the Cloudflare half is ours. The owner's 'we write TypeScript' is what settled it.

decisions.decision: Six new cloudflare symbols to OPEN_FINDINGS, not DISPOSITIONS
decisions.rationale: A disposition says a symbol has a real caller behind a hop the tracer cannot follow; global-object-hop's symbols have callers that RUN. These have a caller in a Worker nothing deploys. Dispositioning would have made the number look like wiring.

decisions.decision: GET /self carries a per-instance marker, and it shipped BEFORE the deploy
decisions.rationale: Criterion 2 needs one PeerId across a construction boundary. Without a marker the owner's four readings cannot show a boundary happened, and yamux's 30s keepalive makes "no boundary" the likely case. A construction-time value rests on nothing platform-specific, unlike the 1012 close-code path whose acceptance by workerd is UNVERIFIED. Added after the deploy it would cost a second deploy, so it had to precede the first.
